title: Custodial Disclosures and the Constitutional Bounds of Evidence
hook: A landmark constitutional ruling established that statutory rules admitting facts discovered from custodial disclosures do not violate the right to equality.
summary:
Following a fatal assault in an agricultural village, an accused individual surrendered before local authorities and voluntarily led investigators to a rural water tank, where a submerged weapon was retrieved. At trial, the prosecution relied on the disclosure statement and physical recovery to establish guilt for murder under the penal code.

The constitutional dispute centered on whether evidentiary provisions permitting statements made exclusively by persons in police custody created an irrational discrimination against persons not in custody. The High Court had struck down the discovery rule as an unconstitutional classification violating the guarantee of equality before the law.

The Supreme Court reversed the invalidation and upheld the statutory discovery rule, holding that persons in police custody constitute a distinct and intelligible class. The court held that the independent corroboration provided by the actual discovery of a physical object guarantees the trustworthiness of the custodial disclosure, ensuring constitutional validity under fundamental rights.
